record.context_brief: dominant maps between very general K3 surfaces
record.original_question: If S is a very general K3 surface with respect to some polarization, does there exist another K3 surface S' not isomorphic to S together with a dominant rational map S → S'?

evidence.quote: (13.2) More generally, if S is a very general K3 surface with respect to some polarization, we ask if there exists another K3 surface S0 not isomorphic to S and a dominant rational map S → S0.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $S$ be a very general complex projective K3 surface with respect to some polarization (that is, $S$ lies outside a countable union of proper subvarieties of the corresponding moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces). Does there exist a complex projective K3 surface $S'$, not isomorphic to $S$, together with a dominant rational map $S \dashrightarrow S'$?
artifact.status_search_result: Closely related results are known: Chen (2010) proved that a very general projective K3 surface admits no dominant self rational map of degree at least two, and Karzhemanov–Konovalov (Israel J. Math., 2024/2025) proved that a very general K3 surface cannot be the target of a non-isomorphic dominant rational map from a smooth projective surface with trivial canonical class. These address related but distinct directions; no source was found that settles the precise question of whether a very general K3 surface can dominate a non-isomorphic K3 surface via a rational map (i.e., with $S$ as source). The status appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Self Rational Maps of K3 Surfaces (Chen)
status_evidence.snippet: A very general projective K3 surface does not admit a dominant self rational map of degree at least two.
status_evidence.claim: Related self-map case resolved; does not answer the question about maps to a non-isomorphic K3.

status_evidence.title: Rational maps and K3 surfaces, Israel J. Math.
status_evidence.snippet: For a very general complex projective K3 surface S and a smooth projective surface A with trivial canonical class, there is no dominant rational map A → S which is not an isomorphism.
status_evidence.claim: Settles the reverse direction (S as target), not the posed question (S as source).
